notes: All text is UTF-8. Hashes: SHA-256 and Keccak-256 as lowercase hex; registry hashes (dataHash, control hashes) are 0x-prefixed.
Canonical JSON: object keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit, no whitespace, ECMAScript number and string printing.
A part is the canonical lines of its winners, sorted by pkHash, each followed by \n.
Head text is the canonical JSON of the head; generation is a decimal string.
Cases with a `question` field follow a provisional reading; see DESIGN-QUESTIONS.md.

namespace.description: K_ns is the HMAC key. ns = first 8 bytes of HMAC-SHA256(K_ns, utf8(message)); keyCheck = first 8 bytes of HMAC-SHA256(K_ns, utf8('key-check')). Registry hashes are keccak256 of the UTF-8 labels, 0x + lowercase hex.

streamMasterKey.description: The stream-sync master key is the 65-byte owner signature as r, low s and v = 27/28. Every encoding gives the same key, so the same K_ns = HKDF-SHA256(masterKey, salt 'vana', info 'scope:' + NAMESPACE_KEY_LABEL, 32), ns and keyCheck. Legacy scope keys keep the raw signature.

buildErrors.why: over 256 UTF-8 bytes, under 256 code units

frames.description: Format 2 frame = envelope LF body LF. Envelope = canonical JSON {h: sha256(body) hex, k: pkHash, n: body bytes, o, r}; body = canonical JSON of the record. A part is frames sorted strictly by k (or the pieces of one long frame). No record size limit.

long.description: Record {"id":"big","x":<count x "a">} as a frame; only digests are listed.

traces.description: A run admitted at g=1 resumes after a delete (v2) and a reconnect elsewhere that committed a g=3 head. chooseBase returns stale_generation; the re-read decides discard and clears checkpoints. Nothing is published, so the g=3 keys stay intact.

traces.name: replay after delete (trace A)
traces.description: Create v1 reply is lost. Another device deletes (v2). The resend is `replayed`. Re-read shows deleted(2): discard, no publish.

traces.name: split run
traces.description: First connect. Stream s1 creates and commits at g=1. Another device deletes (v2), then a reconnect elsewhere makes active(3). Stream s2 must not reconnect or commit at a new generation, and the run saves no checkpoint.

traces.name: split run, delete between streams of a run at g0
traces.description: Run starts with active(1). s1 commits at 1. Another device deletes (v2). s2 discards and clears checkpoints; no checkpoint is saved.

traces.name: stale userConnect entry (trace B)
traces.description: A userConnect run started at deleted(2). Before it publishes, another device reconnects (3) and deletes again (4). The stale entry discards.

no-op onto a complete:false base (ruling Q9)
traces.description: An old DELETE tombstoned s; another device published an empty complete:false head at g=1 and left. This device's incremental run finds nothing new: its parts equal the base and complete stays false, so it is a no-op. The no-op sets needsFull and saves no checkpoint. The next run is full, publishes complete:true, clears needsFull and saves the checkpoint.
